title: AfriBED: a Speech Recognition Bias Evaluation Dataset for Low Resource African Languages
abstract: arXiv:2610.26821v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Despite advancements in automatic speech recognition systems (ASR), current systems exhibit speaker-attribute bias, i.e., their speech recognition performance is biased against certain speakers based on their demographic attributes such as gender, accents, and speaker type. However, accurately assessing speaker attribute bias in a given ASR system requires the availability of a bias evaluation dataset with comparable speech across subgroups of a speaker attribute. In this paper, we introduce African speech Bias Evaluation Dataset (AfriBED), a novel speech recognition bias evaluation dataset for two low resource African languages, Bemba and Nyanja, to detect and estimate gender and speaker-type bias for ASR systems. The dataset comprises 9 hours of speech with 3928 utterances recorded by 80 speakers for Bemba, while the Nyanja set includes 6260 utterances with approximately 18 hours of speech recorded by 127 speakers. translated_title: AfriBED：面向低资源非洲语言的语音识别偏见评估数据集
translated_abstract: 尽管自动语音识别（ASR）系统不断进步，现有系统仍存在说话人属性偏见，即其语音识别性能会因性别、口音和说话人类型等人口统计属性而对某些说话人群体表现出偏见。然而，要准确评估给定ASR系统中的说话人属性偏见，需要拥有一个在说话人属性各子群体之间具有可比语音的偏见评估数据集。本文介绍了非洲语音偏见评估数据集，这是一个面向两种低资源非洲语言——本巴语和尼扬贾语——的新型语音识别偏见评估数据集，用于检测和估计ASR系统的性别偏见和说话人类型偏见。该数据集包含本巴语的9小时语音，由80名说话人录制的3928条语句；尼扬贾语数据集则包含127名说话人录制的6260条语句，约18小时语音。结果表明……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出了面向本巴语和尼扬贾语两种低资源非洲语言的全新语音识别偏见评估数据集AfriBED，可用于检测和估计语音识别系统中的性别偏见与说话人类型偏见。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces AfriBED, a novel speech recognition bias evaluation dataset for two low-resource African languages, Bemba and Nyanja, designed to detect and estimate gender and speaker-type bias in ASR systems.
